item: [C+P] A structure for managing data protection, with a senior person accountable
repo_note: Organisation chart and terms of reference; nothing an architecture sets.

item: [C+P] A DPO where Art 37 requires one (large-scale systematic monitoring or special category data), and supported
repo_note: Background location tracking (32 §9.1) at scale can make a DPO mandatory; decide and record.

item: [C+P] The DPO is independent, has no conflicting role and reports to the top
repo_note: The DPO must not also be the person deciding the processing, such as the CTO.

item: [C+P] Operational roles carry out data protection day to day
repo_note: Named owners exist for packages (28 §1.2), not for personal data.

item: [C+P] An oversight group for data protection and information governance
[C+P] Operational-level groups feed the oversight group
[C+P] Policies and procedures tell staff enough to meet their data protection duties
repo_note: Engineering rules only; no data protection policy for support, sales or operations staff.

item: [C+P] Policies are reviewed and approved so they stay consistent and effective
repo_note: Rule changes go through decision records and review; no data protection policy owner or review date.

item: [C+P] Staff know the policies and procedures that apply to them
[C+P] Policies build in data protection by design and by default
repo_note: Every feature spec asks about personal data and deletion; nothing outside engineering.

item: [C+P] A data protection training programme for all staff
[C+P] Induction and refresher training for everyone
[C+P] Specialist training for roles with key data protection duties
repo_note: Include support staff who can see customer data, and on-call engineers who handle a breach.

item: [C+P] Evidence that staff completed and understood the training
[C+P] Ongoing awareness across the organisation
[C] People are told their rights, and staff recognise a request made verbally or in writing
repo_note: A request need not name the law or come through a form.

item: [C] Enough resource to handle requests
[C] Requests are logged and each one is tracked to closure
repo_note: A ticket queue is enough; it is the evidence of the deadline.

item: [C] Access (Art 15) answered in one month, extendable by two; reasonable and proportionate search; clock stops while clarification is awaited (Art 12A)
repo_note: Person-id references make a search cheap; no rule for finding all of one person's data.

item: [C] Handling of requests is monitored and the results used to improve
[C] Rectification (Art 16): wrong data corrected and incomplete data completed
repo_note: One copy of each fact, referenced by id; no rule that a person can correct their own record.

item: [C] Erasure (Art 17) and objection (Art 21): data deleted, suppressed or no longer processed
repo_note: Deletion list is per customer, not per person; backups, logs, error tracker and devices not covered.

item: [C] Restriction (Art 18): processing of a person's data can be restricted
repo_note: Read-only exists for a whole customer; nothing marks one person's records restricted.

item: [C] Portability (Art 20): a person's data in a structured, machine-readable form
repo_note: Export is a whole-customer hand-over; no per-person export.

item: [C] Automated decisions (Art 22A-22D): information, representations, human intervention, contest
repo_note: No solely automated significant decision as written; a model may not perform a person's legal act.

item: [C] Complaints: an easy route such as an online form, acknowledged within 30 days, outcome without undue delay (DPA 2018 s164A, since 19 June 2026)
repo_note: New duty; tell people they can also complain to the Information Commission.

item: [C] The privacy notice has everything Art 13 and 14 require
repo_note: Notice link in app and store listing, notice per customer; content not specified.

item: [C] People get the notice at the right time: at collection, or within a month for data from elsewhere
repo_note: Disclosure screen before the location prompt; invitation email does not carry the notice.

item: [C] The notice is concise, clear and in plain language for its audience
[C] Automated decision-making and profiling are explained
repo_note: None as written; add a row if a feature scores or ranks people.

item: [C] Front-line staff can explain the privacy information
[C] The notice is reviewed regularly against what the system actually does
repo_note: Trigger a review from the privacy-table diff (06 §6.4).

item: [C] Tools that let people see and control their data, such as a privacy dashboard
repo_note: No rule for a member to see, download or correct their own data.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C+P] A data map: what personal data is held and where
repo_note: Privacy table lists endpoints, deletion list lists stores; no field-level inventory at rest.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C+P] A documented, complete and accurate record of processing activities (ROPA)
repo_note: Inputs exist; no ROPA document. The under-250 exemption does not apply to regular processing.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C+P] The ROPA holds every Art 30 field: Art 30(1) as controller, Art 30(2) per customer as processor
repo_note: Processor record needs each controller, categories of processing, transfers and security measures.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C+P] The ROPA links to contracts, DPIAs, retention and other records
repo_note: Decision records are the natural link target; no rule asks for it.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C] Lawful basis documented and justified per purpose (Art 6), including recognised legitimate interests (Art 6(1)(ea), Annex 1)
repo_note: Account and billing: contract. Annex 1 is a closed list; marketing and security still need the balancing test.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C] Purposes and lawful bases are published
repo_note: In the privacy notice.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C] Where consent is the basis: specific, informed, unbundled, opt-in, recorded and as easy to withdraw
repo_note: Nothing relies on consent as written; the OAuth consent page is not Art 7 consent.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C] Consent records are reviewed and refreshed

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C] Age checks and parental consent where an online service is offered to children (Art 8)
repo_note: No open sign-up; administrators create accounts for adults.

control: Records of processing and lawful basis
item: [C] A legitimate interests assessment for each purpose that relies on legitimate interests
repo_note: Security logging, error reporting, product analytics and B2B prospecting usually need one.

item: [C] Decisions to share personal data with others are managed
repo_note: Personal-data endpoints are off the machine-client list by test; no sharing policy.

item: [C] Data sharing agreements with the controllers data is routinely shared with
[C+P] Restricted transfers follow a procedure
repo_note: See the international transfers section.

item: [C+P] Procedures for the work processors do: hosting, identity, mail, error tracking, crash reports
repo_note: Each vendor is a port with one implementation; no sub-processor register.

item: [C+P] Every controller-processor contract has the Art 28(3) terms, both with customers and with sub-processors
repo_note: Customer DPA and each vendor's DPA; legal, not code.

item: [C+P] Due diligence that each processor has adequate technical and organisational measures
repo_note: Packages are vetted; the services that hold the data are not.

item: [C+P] Processors' compliance with their contracts is reviewed
[C+P] Data protection by design weighs in when choosing services and products
repo_note: Named decision per dependency; no privacy criteria for a SaaS vendor.

item: [C+P] Only the personal data needed goes to processors and third parties
repo_note: No personal data in report context or tags; SDK defaults (IP, breadcrumbs, replay) not addressed.

item: [C+P] Information risks are identified, recorded and managed
repo_note: Threat model per boundary; no risk register.

item: [C+P] Data protection by design and by default (Art 25)
repo_note: Required privacy flag, fail-closed gate, ids not copies, default-off allowlist, non-code tenant barrier.

item: [C] Screening decides whether a DPIA is needed, and records the decision
repo_note: Every feature asks about personal data; no DPIA screening question.

item: [C] DPIAs hold the Art 35(7) content and are documented
repo_note: Template below; keep it beside the threat model.

item: [C] DPIA risks are acted on; high residual risk goes to the Information Commission first (Art 36)
repo_note: Every finding ends in a rule, work item or decision record; nothing on prior consultation.

item: [C+P] Minimum standards for creating records, and records can be found and retrieved
repo_note: Every row has a tenant and branch in its key; no per-person lookup.

item: [C+P] Personal data protected in transit and when sent to another organisation
repo_note: TLS at the edge, authenticated mail; backend TLS not required (33 §6.1).

item: [C+P] Records are accurate, adequate and not excessive (Art 5(1)(c)-(d))
repo_note: Responses minimised and facts held once; no rule against collecting a field nobody needs.

item: [C+P] A retention schedule for all personal data, reviewed regularly (Art 5(1)(e))
repo_note: Log retention enforced by test, TTLs; no schedule for domain data, backups, devices, vendors.

item: [C+P] Destruction methods stop disclosure before, during and after disposal
repo_note: Deletion list includes backups; nothing on device stores or vendor copies.

item: [C+P] An asset register of the systems that store or process personal data
repo_note: Infrastructure code lists cloud resources; vendors and devices missing.

item: [C+P] Acceptable-use rules for software that processes personal data
repo_note: Package admission and data-blind production; no general rules.

item: [C+P] Access limited to authorised staff and reviewed regularly
repo_note: Role gate and audited operator role; no access review.

item: [C+P] Unauthorised access prevented: authentication, vulnerability management, malware protection
repo_note: MFA offered not required; no fix deadline (33 §6.1).

item: [C+P] Risks of mobile devices, remote working and removable media managed
repo_note: Tokens in secure storage; the offline database is not encrypted, staff devices out of scope.

item: [C+P] Physical locations secured
repo_note: Cloud provider for the data centre; offices are the organisation's.

item: [C+P] Continuity plans and backups protect against loss of personal data
repo_note: Deletion protection free, recovery paid; no restore test (33 §7).

item: [C+P] Incidents and personal data breaches are detected, managed and recorded
repo_note: Errors reported, operator actions audited; no security audit trail (33 §6.1).

item: [C] Breaches are assessed and, unless unlikely to risk people, reported to the Information Commission within 72 hours (Art 33)
repo_note: No runbook, owner or contact list.

item: [C] People are told without undue delay when a breach is likely to put them at high risk (Art 34)
repo_note: Needs a contact route per customer and a message template.

item: [C+P] Every breach, reported or not, is logged with facts, effects and remedy (Art 33(5)), and reviewed
repo_note: Lessons become rules and decision records; no breach log.

item: [C+P] External audits or other independent compliance checks
repo_note: Security testing only; no data protection audit.

item: [C+P] An internal audit programme covering data protection
repo_note: Yearly review of all checklists; this one included.

item: [C+P] Business targets for data protection compliance
[C+P] Monitoring results and management information reach senior management
[C+P] Purpose limitation (Art 5(1)(b), compatibility rules in Art 8A): customer data is not reused for the SaaS's own purposes
repo_note: No rule bans analytics, benchmarks or model training on customer data; doing so makes you a controller (Art 28(10)).

item: [C+P] Production personal data is never copied to local or pre-production environments
repo_note: Pre-production data is disposable and seeded via the API; no explicit ban on copying production.

item: [C+P] Accountability (Art 5(2), 24): compliance can be shown with evidence
repo_note: Review results carry evidence; no ROPA or DPIA yet.

item: [C] The data protection fee is paid and the registration kept current
repo_note: Every controller pays unless exempt; the processor role does not remove it.

item: [C+P] Security of processing (Art 32): risk-based measures, encryption, resilience, restore, regular testing
repo_note: Encryption at rest and yearly testing; no restore test, backend TLS or offline-store encryption.

item: [P] Personal data is processed only on the customer's documented instructions, and staff do not browse it (Art 29)
repo_note: Production is data-blind and operator reads audited; the instructions are the contract.

item: [P] People who can reach customer data are bound to confidentiality
[P] Sub-processors only with the customer's authorisation; changes notified in advance; terms flowed down
repo_note: No sub-processor list; identity, mail, hosting, error and crash reporting all qualify.

item: [P] Tools that let the customer answer rights requests: find, export, correct, restrict and erase one person
repo_note: Whole-customer export and delete only.

item: [P] The customer gets help with security, breaches, DPIAs and prior consultation (Art 32-36)
repo_note: Checklist results and threat model are the pack; no DPIA input document.

item: [P] At the end of the contract, data is returned and then deleted, copies included
repo_note: Hand-over of the customer's database, then the tested deletion list.

item: [P] Information and audits that show compliance are available to the customer
repo_note: Tracker with evidence per row; no customer-facing trust pack.

item: [P] The customer is told of a breach without undue delay (Art 33(2))
repo_note: Controller recorded per customer; no breach contact or procedure. Your delay spends their 72 hours.

item: [P] One customer's data never reaches another customer
repo_note: A barrier that is not code, tenant from the verified claim, isolation tests.

item: [C+P] Where every store, backup, log and vendor holds personal data, and who can reach it from abroad, is known
repo_note: No rule pins a region; vendor support access from abroad is a transfer too.

item: [C+P] Each restricted transfer has a mechanism: UK adequacy regulations (UK-US data bridge for certified US firms), or the IDTA or the EU SCCs with the UK Addendum
repo_note: Contract terms; existing IDTAs and Addenda still work, but the ICO plans DUAA updates to both.

item: [C+P] The data protection test is met and recorded: protection not materially lower than in the UK
repo_note: The statutory name for the transfer risk assessment; one decision record per vendor fits.

item: [P] As processor, transfers happen only as the customer's contract allows
[C+P] Keys, data-blind operation and minimal vendor payloads limit what a transfer exposes
repo_note: Customer-managed keys for the data that needs them; no rule ties this to transfers.

control: PECR: device storage and electronic marketing
item: [C] Storage on or access to a device (cookies, local storage, app storage, SDK identifiers) only when exempt or consented
repo_note: The token in browser storage is strictly necessary; no inventory of what clients and SDKs store.

control: PECR: device storage and electronic marketing
item: [C] Analytics and appearance storage use the DUAA exceptions only for that sole purpose, with clear information and a free, simple way to object
repo_note: Error and crash SDKs store identifiers and may replay sessions; no rule says which exception applies.

control: PECR: device storage and electronic marketing
item: [C] Consent, where needed, is asked before storage, with refusal as easy as acceptance
repo_note: Nothing needs consent as written; this becomes a row when a marketing tag is added.

control: PECR: device storage and electronic marketing
item: [C] Marketing email and texts to individuals (including sole traders and partnerships) have consent or the soft opt-in, identify the sender and offer a free opt-out
repo_note: Corporate addresses are outside reg 22 but a named person's address is still personal data.

control: PECR: device storage and electronic marketing
item: [C] Service emails (invitations, codes, resets) carry no marketing
repo_note: Templates are transactional by design; no rule keeps promotion out.

control: PECR: device storage and electronic marketing
item: [C+P] Opt-outs are honoured for good and kept per sender
repo_note: Suppression list per customer; an opt-out is kept off the tool list.
